paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God finishes what He starts. He says of Gog's fall, "Yes, it is coming, and it will surely happen, declares the Lord GOD." (Ezekiel 39:8) Gog comes against Israel, but God is the One who turns him around and drives him along (Ezekiel 39:2). So when a threat looks bigger than everything, the baker can remember who is really in charge.

Now look at WHY God does all of this. Again and again He says people will know that He is the LORD, and that He will make His holy name known and will no longer allow it to be profaned (Ezekiel 39:7). He even tells the nations why Israel went into exile: "they were unfaithful to Me." (Ezekiel 39:23) God doesn't hide that. I think that's honest love, because He names the hurt and still doesn't walk away.

And then comes that big "Therefore." God says, "Now I will restore Jacob from captivity and will have compassion on the whole house of Israel…" (Ezekiel 39:25) He promises not to leave any of them behind (Ezekiel 39:28), and to pour out His Spirit on them (Ezekiel 39:29). I sat in the back of a drawer for years thinking I was done, and I know what it's like to be found, friend. If you've drifted, God's compassion is bigger than your worst chapter, and He keeps His promises. That's why my ovens stay ready.
